name: rebel-bot-swarm
description: A dashboard for your Claude Code team: open your team leader in a new chat, status, original avatars, who is working on what, live progress, comms lines, member brains, Save team / Restore team. Local only.

rebelBotSwarm.boardFile.markdownDescription: Optional team board (Markdown) with `## Sessions`, `## Files being edited`, a `## ... slot` table and `## Waiting ...` list. See the guide in `docs/`. `~` = your home folder.

rebelBotSwarm.privateMembers.description: Members (name or part of a name) whose messages stay hidden. Their status still shows.

rebelBotSwarm.refreshSeconds.description: How often the open panel reads the session files.

enumDescriptions: Sessions started in the open workspace folders
All live Claude Code sessions on this computer

rebelBotSwarm.avatarsFolder.description: Folder of your own pictures (.png .jpg .webp .svg) named after members; Upload picture copies new ones here. Empty = VS Code's storage folder for this extension.

rebelBotSwarm.requestsFolder.markdownDescription: Folder for the request files from **Add team member** and the edit panel (task and role instructions), for your coordinator session to read. Empty = VS Code's storage folder for this extension (command **Rebel Bot Swarm: Open requests folder**). `~` = your home folder.

rebelBotSwarm.membersFile.markdownDescription: File that keeps the names and avatars you choose in the edit panel (JSON; a backup is made before each change). Empty = `members.json` in VS Code's storage folder for this extension. `~` = your home folder.

rebelBotSwarm.showUnnamedSessions.markdownDescription: Show a card for a live session that still has its default title (the project-folder name, for example `my-project` or `my-project-e4`) and is not on the board. Off = such sessions are hidden.

rebelBotSwarm.condenseTokens.markdownDescription: A member card highlights its **Condense** button when that chat's context is this many tokens or more (read from the last reply in the chat transcript). The button also lights up when the board job says done.

rebelBotSwarm.condensePrompt.default:
BRAIN SAVE before {action}. You are {member}. Before this chat is {actionPast}, write what you learned on your last task to your brain: your memory files (MEMORY.md and its notes) or the team wiki, as your own rules say. Add one log line for the job, and each MISTAKE: and LESSON: line. Write the state of any open work so that a fresh chat can continue it. Do not start new work.
When this is done, reply with ONE line: "BRAIN SAVED - you can {actionNext} now."
rebelBotSwarm.condensePrompt.markdownDescription: The prompt that **Condense** puts on the clipboard (and in the member's chat box when the chat is not open), so the member saves its lessons to its brain first. `{member}`, `{action}` (condense / restart), `{actionPast}` (condensed / restarted), `{actionNext}` (type /compact / close this chat and start a new one). Empty = the default text.

rebelBotSwarm.decidePrompt.default:
You are {leader}, {leaderRole}. I want to decide this open item from the team board ({board}): '{item}'.
Read the board file (and any file the item names) for context. Explain the choice in 3-5 short lines, then ask me the decision as ONE multiple-choice question (2-4 options, the recommended option first).
Record my answer: if you are the board's owner or coordinator, append one dated line to the board's log; else write ONE file "DECISION <yyyy-mm-dd HHMMSS>.json" in {requestsFolder} with {"type": "decision", "item": "<the item>", "answer": "<my answer>", "from": "Decide"}.
Keep this chat short. At the end, tell me in one line that I can close this tab.
rebelBotSwarm.decidePrompt.markdownDescription: The prompt that **Decide ▸** (on each *Waiting for you* item) puts in a new Claude Code chat. `{leader}`, `{leaderRole}`, `{item}` = the item text, `{board}` = the board file, `{requestsFolder}` = the requests folder. Empty = the default text.

rebelBotSwarm.agentCards.markdownDescription: Also show a **ready** card for each agent file in `~/.claude/agents/` that has no card yet (name from the file name, job from its `description:` line).

rebelBotSwarm.brainsFolder.markdownDescription: Folder for member brain files (`<member>.md`) shown in the edit panel, when Claude Code's own subagent memory (`memory:` in the agent file) is not used. Empty = VS Code's storage folder for this extension. `~` = your home folder.

rebelBotSwarm.leaderSessionId.markdownDescription: The session id of your team leader's own Claude Code chat (the file name of its transcript in `~/.claude/projects/<project>/`, without `.jsonl`). **Decide ▸** puts the question in this chat. Empty = the newest chat whose tab title starts with the leader name. If no chat is found, Decide opens a new chat. Decide always also writes a `DECIDE <time>.json` request file in the requests folder.

rebelBotSwarm.leaderName.markdownDescription: The name of your team leader. The **OPEN** button opens a new chat as this leader (it says "Hi, I am <name>"), the OPEN button shows the name on the leader's card, and the dashboard shows the leader as a card (the board row or member with this name, else the row whose job says coordinator). Example: `Ada`.

rebelBotSwarm.leaderRole.markdownDescription: The role of your team leader, used in the starter prompt of the OPEN button ("You are <name>, <role> of my Rebel Bot Swarm team").

name.description: Team name, for example Red or Website

leader.description: Name of the card that leads this team, for example Red Leader

scope.description: Optional short line: what this team works on

color.description: Team colour as #rrggbb, shown on the team header and on each of its cards

parent.description: Optional: the team this one is a sub-team of (one level), for example Security under Website

rebelBotSwarm.teams.markdownDescription: Teams inside the swarm (max 12). Each team has a `name`, an optional `leader` (the name of the card that leads it) and an optional `scope` line shown on its header an optional `color` (#rrggbb) shown on its header and cards, and an optional `parent` (the team it is a sub-team of, one level). Example: `[{"name": "Website", "leader": "Ada", "scope": "site pages, blog, downloads"}]`. A member joins a team in its card's edit panel. User settings only, so every VS Code window shows the same teams. The swarm leader (`leaderName`) stays above all teams.

rebelBotSwarm.roles.markdownDescription: The roles you can pick for a member in its edit panel. "Team leader" is always there.

rebelBotSwarm.team.markdownDescription: Show ONE team in this window: set it in the **Workspace** settings (for example `Website`). The dashboard then shows that team and the swarm leader, and **Spark** starts that team's leader. Empty = the whole swarm.

rebelBotSwarm.sparkPrompt.default:
You are {leader}, {leaderRole} of my Rebel Bot Swarm team of Claude Code members. First say only: "Hi, I'm {leader}. What would you like to do?" and wait for my answer.
Then route the task, and do not do the work yourself:
1. If an agent file in {agentsFolder} fits the task, hand the task to that member with the Agent tool (subagent_type = the agent's name) and give it a short, clear brief.
2. If no member fits, or the task is for the coordinator, write ONE request file "REQUEST <yyyy-mm-dd HHMMSS>.json" in {requestsFolder} with {"type": "request", "task": "<the task>", "from": "Spark"}.
{board}Ask at most one question if the task is not clear. Keep this chat short.
At the end, tell me in one line who has the task, and that I can close this tab: the Rebel Bot Swarm dashboard keeps the status.
rebelBotSwarm.sparkPrompt.markdownDescription: The starter prompt that the **OPEN** button puts in a new Claude Code chat (you press Enter to send it). `{agentsFolder}` = `~/.claude/agents`, `{requestsFolder}` = the requests folder, `{leader}` = the leader name, `{leaderRole}` = the leader role, `{board}` = one line about your board file (empty if no board is set). Empty = the default text.

walkthroughs.title: Start here: Rebel Bot Swarm
walkthroughs.description: Four steps to run your Claude Code team from the dashboard.

steps.title: 1. Open and close the dashboard
steps.description:
Click **Swarm** in the status bar (bottom left) to open the dashboard; click it again to close it. Or use the **Rebel Bot Swarm** icon in the activity bar (left edge), the keys **Ctrl+Alt+S** (Windows, Linux), or the command **Rebel Bot Swarm: Toggle dashboard**.
[Open the dashboard](command:rebelBotSwarm.show)

steps.title: 2. Press OPEN to start work
steps.description:
**OPEN** (it shows your leader's name) opens a new Claude Code chat with a starter prompt in the chat box. Press Enter, then say what you want to do. The chat hands the task to the right member.
[Spark a new chat](command:rebelBotSwarm.spark)

steps.title: 3. Close chat tabs when the job is handed over
steps.description: You do not need to keep the chat open. The dashboard keeps watching your team and shows who is working, who is waiting for you and who is done.

steps.title: 4. Save team to keep your pictures and names safe
steps.description:
Your names, pictures and panel brains are in VS Code's storage folder, which can be deleted when you uninstall. **Save team** writes one .zip file where you choose. **Restore team** puts it back.
[Save team](command:rebelBotSwarm.saveTeam)
